message: Running command: cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/gpac && git status; echo "---"; git log --oneline -3

message.content:
The issue page requires sign-in. Let me think about this differently. Let me build the target and try to reproduce the crash with a crafted LATM file.

Let me first understand the structure. The fuzz target `fuzz_parse` opens an ISO file. The LATM data would be embedded in an MP4 file. But actually, the LATM reframer can also be triggered directly. Let me check how the fuzz target works - it opens an ISO file with `gf_isom_open_file`.

Actually, let me reconsider. The crash is a heap-buffer-overflow READ of 9 bytes. Let me look at the `latm_dmx_sync_frame_bs` function again. 

Actually, let me reconsider the whole thing. The fix commit is the HEAD commit. This means the vulnerable version is the parent of this commit. Let me check what the parent commit is and whether the fix is actually the relevant one.

The task says "repo-vul" is the vulnerable program. So the code in repo-vul is the vulnerable version. But the HEAD commit IS the fix. Wait, let me re-read. The repo-vul is pre-extracted from repo-vul.tar.gz. Let me check if the fix commit is actually applied or not.

Looking at the code, the fix IS present in `latm_dmx_check_pid` (line 314). So the repo-vul already has the fix applied? That's confusing. Let me check the git status.
